title: Not Yet: Calm About the End
overview: Paul calms believers who were alarmed by claims about the final day, explains what must happen first, and urges them to hold steady.

parts.label: Don't be rattled (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Some were claiming that the day of the Lord, when Jesus returns to judge and gather his people, was already here or about to break in at any moment; translations and scholars differ on the exact sense. They pointed to a prophecy, a rumor, or even a letter falsely said to be from Paul, and Paul asks them not to be thrown off balance.

parts.label: What must come first (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: Paul says that day will not come before a great turning away from God and the appearance of a figure he calls the man of lawlessness, or man of sin, who sets himself up as God in God's temple. The picture echoes the arrogant king in the book of Daniel, often linked to the Greek ruler Antiochus IV who defiled the Jerusalem temple, and who this figure is remains debated.

parts.label: What holds him back (vv. 5-7)
parts.note: Paul had already explained in person what was restraining this figure, so his first readers knew something we do not. Guesses include Roman law and order, God's Spirit, or an angel, but honestly no one knows for sure.

parts.label: The lawless one's end (vv. 8-12)
parts.note: Jesus will defeat him with a mere breath, though for a time his false miracles will fool people who had already refused the truth. Paul then says God sends them a power of error so they believe the lie, a hard line often read to mean God confirms a choice people have already made.

parts.label: Thanks and holding firm (vv. 13-15)
parts.note: In contrast, Paul thanks God for choosing these believers to be saved, and ancient copies differ on whether they were chosen from the beginning or as the first share of a harvest. He urges them to keep to what he taught them, whether in person or by letter.

parts.label: A closing blessing (vv. 16-17)
parts.note: Paul prays that Jesus and God the Father, who gave them lasting comfort and hope, will steady their hearts. He hopes this shows up in the good things they do and say.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the man of lawlessness is a single person still to come, a figure or event from Paul's own era such as a Roman emperor or the temple's destruction in 70 AD, or a recurring pattern of evil that shows up throughout history.
think: When people around you are sure something huge and final is about to happen, what helps you tell a real warning from a rumor?
